text: There goes the ferry. Right on time. [dryly] The captain was always a stickler for the timetable. And for the safety announcement.
Ferry's passing. I'm waving. [to Gerrit] You could wave too, you know. You've got the wings for it.
[quietly] That's the ferry horn. Volume up a notch, in case the captain's got the radio on in the wheelhouse.
Hear that horn? Somewhere on that ferry, somebody's reading the safety announcement. Same words as ever. [amused] Not on this station.
[quietly] Hear that? Container ship, going by out on the deep water. Felt that one in the floorboards.
That foghorn's the lowest note you'll hear on Radio Alles. [dryly] Better bass than half the records.
Big container ship passing. In a few minutes her wake gets here and everything on the shelf goes sideways. [to Gerrit] Hold on to your crate.
[raising his voice] Hang on... there's a tall ship out there. Full sail, every one of them set. If you're near a window, look.
A tall ship, going by under sail. No engine, no generator to keep coughing. [wistful] Just wind. I'm not jealous. Much.
Tall ship off the island. [mock-serious] If she's come for the station, she's welcome to Gerrit.
[quietly] That was a whale. Blowing, just off the point. I'll keep the talking down a minute.
A whale just came up for air out there. [amused] Gerrit's gone very still. I think he's worked out he's not the biggest thing at sea.
There's a whale out there, somewhere near. I sometimes wonder what it makes of the transmitter. [dryly] It hasn't written in.
Dolphins! A whole pod, going past the bow. [warmly] They don't stop. They never stop. Busy people, dolphins.
Dolphins off the starboard side. [to Gerrit] No, you can't have one.
There's a pod of dolphins going by, and they're keeping better time than the drummer on this record.
[clears throat] There's... a light over the island. Moving. I'm not going to speculate on air. Next record.
Whatever that is over the island, it's not on any frequency I know. [deadpan] Another unlicensed broadcaster, probably. Good luck to them.
[quietly] Gerrit saw that too. He's looking at me. I'm looking at him. Neither of us is going to say it.
Fireworks over the island. Somebody's celebrating something. [warmly] Good. Somebody should.
[to Gerrit] It's fireworks, Gerrit. Come out from under the tarp. Nobody's shooting at you.
Fireworks going up, and the whole lot doubled in the water. [quietly] Best seat on the island, and it isn't even on the island.
Shooting star, right over the lighthouse. [dryly] I wished for a new part for Opa. Romantic, me.
[raising his voice] There, a shooting star! Gone. If you missed it, the sky's still up there. Keep looking.
A shooting star just went across. [quietly] I'll leave the next record to say something about that.
[quietly] Go to a window. Northern lights over the island. Green, moving. I've no words, so here's a record.
The northern lights are out. It's freezing on deck and I'm out there anyway. [sniffs] Back to the records in a minute.
Northern lights over the lighthouse. [wistful] The lamp's going round under all that green, like it's trying to keep up.
There goes the lamp. The lighthouse is on for the night. [warmly] Evening, keeper.
First sweep of the lamp just crossed the wheelhouse. Every time, I look up. Every time, I'm glad.
Lamp's on. The keeper's light does the night shift now. [dryly] Mine just does the records.
The lighthouse is lit. [to Gerrit] That's your cue to stop staring at the mainland and come in.
The lamp's just gone off up at the lighthouse. It's done its night. [quietly] Mine goes on a bit longer.
Lighthouse lamp's off. That's a night survived, on the island and on the Zeemeeuw. [dryly] Kettle.
Lamp's off, and Gerrit's up on the aerial, shaking himself out. Static for a minute. Bear with us.
[quietly] It's started snowing. Big slow flakes past the wheelhouse window. Leave the records running, I'm just going to watch.
Snow! [to Gerrit] Don't look at me like that. I didn't order it.
First flakes are coming down on the deck. Opa's going to need his blanket tonight.
That's the siren test on the island. Noon, first Monday of the month. [dryly] Nothing to worry about, unless you're Gerrit.
The island siren. [mock-serious] Still the loudest thing on air today, and they don't even have a licence for music.
Siren test. Twelve o'clock, then. [amused] Between that and the ferry, I've never once needed a watch.
[quietly] The keeper's lit the campfire. I can hear the guitar across the water. Let's give him a minute.
Guitar on the shore. The keeper's got it out again. [amused] He's a bit behind the record I'm playing, but he's catching up.
Campfire's going and there's a guitar drifting over. [dryly] Keeper, if you take requests, I'll row a note over.
